1 .  By way of present application, the appellant seeks suspension of sentence during the pendency of the appeal.

2. By way of present appeal, the appellant seeks to assail the judgement of conviction dated 09.02.2024 and order on sentence 22.04.2025 vide which he has been convicted and sentenced to undergo SI for 7 years with fine of Rs.50,000/- for the offence under Section 304B and further sentenced to undergo SI for 1 year with fine of Rs.10,000/- for the offence under Section 498A IPC.
Benefit of section 428 Cr.P.C. was directed to be given to the appellant.

As per the initial statement recorded during inquest proceedings by the SDM, the demand of Rs.5 lacs by the appellant is stated to have been made through one Dr. Surender Kumar Sharma, who however, during his deposition, was declared hostile.

He further submits that the husband of the deceased was acquitted by the Trial Court which found finding no allegation qua Ashok Sharma vs State Of Delhi on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147728752/

sentences.text:
It is further contended that the testimony of the brother of the deceased has considerable improvements in his statements made during the inquest, and confrontations in this regard were made at the time of cross- examination.
4.
Learned APP for the State has opposed the bail application.
He contends that the death has taken place within two and a half months of the marriage.
5. I have heard the learned counsels for the parties and perused the records.
Nominal roll of the appellant is also placed on record as per which, as on 09.07.2025 the appellant is aged about 74 years and has undergone sentence of about 2 years by now.

Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, the sentence of the appellant is directed to be suspended during the pendency of appeal on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court/Duty Judicial Magistrate/Link Judicial Magistrate/Jail Superintendent and also subject to the further following conditions:-
(i) In case of change of residential address, the appellant shall promptly inform the same to the concerned Investigating Officer as well as to this Court.
(ii) The appellant shall regularly appear before the Court as This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 02/09/2025 at 22:46:45 and when the appeal is taken up for hearing.
6. With the above directions, the application is disposed of.
7. A copy of this order be communicated electronically forthwith to the concerned Jail Superintendent for information and necessary compliance.
List in due course.
MANOJ KUMAR OHRI, J SEPTEMBER 2, 2025 ga
